A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EvRT-DETR research, despite the changed title and I2EvDet framing. All 11 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gen1 and Gen4 detection results, YOLOX comparisons, and augmentation, temporal-module, interpolation, and clip-length ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds runtime reporting, parameter counts, a qualitative detection sequence, and a finding about learnable residual scaling.

M1.justification: V2's formulation introduces learnable ReZero-style residual weighting in Equation 4. However, Appendix A.2 specifies fixed scaling of 1.0 for the implemented model. The frozen RT-DETR, three ConvLSTM modules, two-stage training, and reduced-width output projections already appear in v1; I2EvDet is largely a broader formulation of that design.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gen1 and Gen4 automotive detection datasets and object classes; 1Mpx is explicitly another name for Gen4. V2's stopped-camera illustration uses retained benchmark coverage rather than introducing a new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: V1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1 contain the same comparison methods, including ERGO-12, SAST-CB, RVT-B, and S5-ViT-B. The YOLOX-T/S/L/X comparison is retained unchanged from v1 Table 4 in v2 Table 8.

E3.justification: V2 replaces FLOPS reporting with runtime evaluation standardized to NVIDIA T4, including FLOPS/throughput conversion of timings from other hardware. The retained accuracy experiments keep their event windows, resolutions, training budgets, clip lengths, and COCO metrics. Omitted preprocessing details do not establish that preprocessing actually changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds a stopped-camera detection case study in Figure 4 and reports that learnable residual scaling provides no measurable Gen1 benefit in Appendix A.2. Parameter counts extend the existing capacity analysis. The kernel, placement, augmentation, interpolation, and clip-length ablations were already present in v1, including its appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its experiments. References to significant improvements do not introduce statistical procedures.

E6.justification: V2 adds a full runtime comparison, including EvRT-DETR-B timings of 12.7 ms on Gen1 and 18.8 ms on 1Mpx. Table 4 adds temporal-module parameter counts of 2.3, 5.4, 14.4, and 42.9 million; S5-ViT-B's total changes from 18.2 to 17.5 million. New qualitative findings supplement these efficiency results. All matched benchmark and ablation accuracy values remain unchanged, including 52.7/50.1 mAP for EvRT-DETR-B.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 4 generalizes v1's unit-weight residual equation with a scaling parameter. The explicit projection equations largely formalize dimensional projections already documented in v1 Appendix B.3. The event-histogram definition remains equivalent, and no new theorem, proof, or formal memory guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution broadens from adapting RT-DETR specifically for event cameras to I2EvDet as a general framework for converting image detectors into video-capable models, with potential applications across temporal visual domains. V2 also adds competitive inference speed to its contribution claims. The benchmark superiority claims and stated accuracy margins remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting kernel size to spatial context, lower-level temporal features to motion detail, and longer clips to object persistence. It emphasizes transformer advantages in the retained YOLOX comparison. V1's explicit cautions about heterogeneous runtime measurements are replaced by claims of fair T4-standardized comparison and practical inference speed.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies internal input projection and fixed residual scaling, but removes v1's YOLOX implementation commit and inference thresholds of 0.65/0.01. Exact split sizes and the disclosure that all Gen4 frame annotations are retained also disappear. Core training hyperparameters, software versions, training hardware, and the project code link remain available.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantive model-adaptation subsection connecting the work to parameter-efficient transfer learning, including Houlsby adapters, unified transfer-learning work, QLoRA, and convolutional LoRA. This supports repositioning the contribution as a general adaptation framework beyond v1's mainly event-representation and detector discussion. SAM 2 and the separate YOLOX repository reference are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around I2EvDet. RT-DETR background moves into related work, temporal-module ablations move from the appendix into the main evaluation, and augmentation and YOLOX discussions move into the appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the simple architecture diagram with a detailed temporal framework illustration and adds an accuracy-runtime plot, event-frame examples, and a detection-sequence comparison. Tables are relocated and restyled, captions expand, and the capacity table gains a trainable-parameter column. These changes substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves visual explanation and makes parameter costs and temporal detection behavior more concrete through Table 4 and Figure 4. However, it removes useful reproducibility details and replaces v1's runtime-comparability cautions with stronger fairness claims based partly on hardware-throughput conversions, without documenting controls addressing the earlier concerns. The unchanged accuracy evidence does not resolve this tradeoff between clearer presentation and weaker methodological disclosure, so a reliable net quality judgment is not possible.
